cmqwkg6hy00yfnwqo8yw23tg7.overview: The field of Stress Management focuses on understanding stressors and developing strategies to cope with them. This program is ideal for individuals interested in mental health, wellness, and personal development. Students engage in interactive learning experiences, gaining insights into stress theories, techniques, and their applications in real-world scenarios.
cmqwkg6hy00yfnwqo8yw23tg7.entry: Applicants must be in the final year of high school or have graduated, and meet YÖK's rules for admission from abroad (Turkish and TRNC citizens only in the cases the directive lists). You qualify with a high-school diploma at the minimum in the directive's Annex-1 country table (a 50% diploma grade for many national certificates; at least 50% if your country is not in the table) — or, instead, one of these exam results: SAT 1000/1600 with at least 550 in each of Math and Critical Reading, ACT 26/36, IB 30/45, or two A Levels at grade D or above in relevant subjects. School-leaving exams (Abitur, IB, GCE, Tawjihi) have no validity limit; university-entrance exams such as SAT are valid for two years. The International Relations Department evaluates applications within quotas (ranked by graduation GPA if oversubscribed) and may hold an interview; special-talent programmes follow their own exam rules.
cmqwkg6hy00yfnwqo8yw23tg7.language: An English certificate is not required to apply. For English-taught programmes, PTE Academic 55, TOEFL iBT 72 (Home Edition not accepted), CAE / FCE / CPE grade C, e-TEP 74, Cambridge Linguaskill 145, YDS/e-YDS/YÖKDİL 70, or 60 in the FBU Proficiency exam exempts you from English prep; the unit board may exempt citizens of countries where English is an official language. Otherwise the English preparatory class (fee equal to the programme's annual tuition).
documents: Valid passport
High-school diploma or graduation certificate (English or Turkish)
High-school transcript for all years (English or Turkish)
